validity.recommendation: Existence and as-built specs (1301 km, commissioned Jan 1952, Dashava field origin) are well-documented historically -- no red flag on the pipeline being real.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed, independent of GEM/gem.wiki. This is one of the USSR's first two long-distance gas trunks (after Saratov-Moscow). Two independent, non-GEM sources -- BBC Ukrainian (Oct 2018, https://www.bbc.com/ukrainian/blog-history-russian-45706179) and Russian Wikipedia's 'Дашава — Киев' article (uncited/tertiary but predates the BBC piece and shows no citation chain to it) -- both independently state: original Dashava-Kyiv section opened 1 Oct 1948, length 509.6 km, pipe diameter 500 mm nominal, design throughput 1,500,000 m3/day; extended through Bryansk to Moscow, new section commissioned 18 Jan 1952, TOTAL length Dashava-Kyiv-Moscow = 1301 km (exact match to GEM's LengthKnown=1301.00). This matches GEM's StartYear1=1952 and LengthKnown=1301 exactly. FuelSource='Dashava Gas Field' is correct for the pipeline's original design purpose (both sources describe it repeatedly as carrying gas from the Dashava field). Checked the sheet's own cited energybase.ru page (wiki_citations.json) -- it is IP/geo-blocked from this environment (confirmed via url_verifier: 200 but 'access-block interstitial', not a 404, so NOT a dead-link deletion candidate, just unusable here) and has zero Wayback captures at any URL variant, so it could not be used to corroborate; the two sources above substitute as independent corroboration instead. Duplicate check against the 39-pipeline roster: no other row shares Dashava as an origin or Bryansk/Moscow as a destination; this is not a duplicate of any other GGIT Ukraine row. It IS, however, now interconnected with two roster pipelines (see the classification concern below): P1452 (Shebelinka-Poltava-Kiev) per BBC, and P2387 (Shebelinka-Belgorod-Kursk-Bryansk) per ru.wikipedia -- flagging for awareness, not as duplicates (distinct physical corridors).

validity.recommendation: Update should re-examine PipelineType, EndLocation and FuelSource in light of the 1966 reversal: BOTH BBC and ru.wikipedia state that in 1966 this pipeline's flow was PHYSICALLY REVERSED and it stopped functioning as a Dashava-to-Moscow transmission corridor. Recommend either (a) updating PipelineType to reflect the current distribution role and EndLocation/EndCountryOrArea to reflect current Ukraine-only service (Kyiv/Zhytomyr/Ternopil oblasts per BBC), with a ResearcherNotes entry documenting the pre-/post-1966 history, or (b) at minimum adding a ResearcherNotes caveat if the row is deliberately kept as the historical as-built corridor. Do not silently leave PipelineType='transmission' and EndLocation=Moscow/Russia unexamined -- both are now stale claims about current function, not just possibly-imprecise history.
validity.researcher_notes: MAJOR FINDING, not previously flagged in this row's history per the country note. Both BBC Ukrainian (2018) and ru.wikipedia's 'Дашава — Киев' article independently state: 'До 1966 года газопровод Дашава-Киев-Москва работал в восточном направлении. Но с открытием других мощных месторождений ситуация изменилась. Подземную магистраль подключили к первой нитке другого газопровода - Шебелинка-Полтава-Киев. Он стал работать как распределительный. После реконструкции шлейфов на компрессорных станциях газ пошел по трубам в обратном направлении - на запад.' (Until 1966 the pipeline ran eastward; after other gas fields opened it was connected to the Shebelinka-Poltava-Kyiv line and reconstructed to run WEST instead, becoming a DISTRIBUTION pipeline.) BBC states the pipeline currently (as of 2018) supplies natural gas to towns/villages of Kyiv, Zhytomyr and Ternopil oblasts -- i.e. its documented CURRENT function is a Ukraine-domestic western distribution asset, not a Dashava-to-Moscow transmission line. Independently, ru.wikipedia corroborates the 1966 reversal-to-distribution and additionally notes a 1959 interconnection with the 'Shebelinka-Belgorod-Kursk-Bryansk' pipeline (= roster P2387) feeding gas onward to Belarus/Lithuania/Latvia via the Bryansk-Moscow section. So since 1966 the row's two halves have functioned as separate systems: the Ukrainian half is a west-flowing regional distribution line (fed by the Shebelinka network, P1452/P2387), and the Bryansk-Moscow half in Russia is part of Gazprom/Mostransgaz's own Moscow-region gas ring (documented at length in that company's internal history publication, Gazprom Transgaz Moskva's 'Prometei' newsletter -- content reviewed for research leads via a Wayback capture but its PDF text failed automated url_verifier text-matching, likely because the archived PDF is a scanned/rasterized layout the verifier's simple text search doesn't parse cleanly, so it is NOT included in proposed_refs per the verify-before-cite rule; not asserting it's unusable, just unverifiable by the mechanical gate here). GEM's row bundles both eras/halves under one still-'operating', 'transmission', Moscow-terminating record with no note of the 1966 change. I am NOT calling this a duplicate or a phantom -- the physical pipe is real and (per BBC) still in service -- but the CURRENT classification/location/fuel-source triad looks stale relative to the sourced 1966 reconfiguration and deserves a human Update pass rather than a silent pass-through.

validity.recommendation: GTSOU (Owner2) is well-supported as the correct Ukrainian-side owner/operator since the 2020 unbundling. Gazprom PJSC (Owner1) is unverified for this specific pipeline and, combined with the classification finding above (the pipeline's documented current function is Ukraine-domestic distribution, not a live cross-border transmission link), is a live attribution question rather than a settled fact -- flag per the country-note standing rule on Gazprom-as-Ukraine-owner rather than silently keeping it.
validity.researcher_notes: Owner1='Gazprom PJSC', Owner2='Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine', no percentages given. Verified https://web.archive.org/web/20250421144750/https://tsoua.com/en/about-us/key-facts/ (this is literally the same page the gem.wiki citation list already references, cite_note-:4-2) confirms: 'LLC Gas TSO of Ukraine ... Starting from January 1, 2020, LLC Gas TSO of Ukraine is the certified operator of the gas transmission system of Ukraine and fully independent of vertically integrated undertakings. October 27, 2023 – ... 100% of the GTSOU's equity stake was transferred to the Ministry of Energy of Ukraine.' This directly supports Owner2 as the correct current Ukrainian-side entity (state-owned via the Ministry of Energy since Oct 2023, per the country note's standing framework). However I could not find any citable, verifiable source assigning Gazprom PJSC a specific ownership share of THIS named pipeline. The country-note standing rule states a row recording Gazprom as owner is an attribution concern when the pipeline lies wholly inside Ukraine, with the correct reading on a genuinely cross-border row being a Ukraine/Russia split. This row is nominally cross-border (Dashava, Ukraine -> Moscow, Russia) which would normally justify the split as-is -- BUT the classification finding above shows the pipeline has not functioned as a live Dashava-Moscow through-line since 1966; its documented current role is a Ukraine-domestic distribution asset serving Kyiv/Zhytomyr/Ternopil oblasts. That undercuts the premise for keeping Gazprom PJSC as a co-owner of what is, in current practice, a Ukrainian distribution pipeline. Recommend Update research the specific legal owner of the Bryansk-Moscow section (likely a Gazprom transgaz Moskva / Mostransgaz-type subsidiary per that company's own 70th-anniversary history publication, not the PJSC parent directly) and re-examine whether Gazprom should remain listed against this row at all given the 1966 functional split.

validity.recommendation: Recommend converting Diameter/DiameterUnits to the metric figure the sources actually state (500 mm nominal / ~529-530 mm actual OD) rather than the current '20.87 in' -- the number itself is not wrong (20.87 in = 529.9 mm, consistent with sourced 500-529 mm), but no source anywhere states an inch figure; this is a lossy unit round-trip with fabricated precision, matching the pattern the orchestrator already flagged for this exact row.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM stores Diameter=20.87, DiameterUnits='in'. 20.87 in x 25.4 = 529.9 mm. Both BBC ('использовали широкие трубы диаметром 500 мм' -- used wide pipe of 500 mm diameter) and ru.wikipedia ('диаметр трубы — 500 мм') independently give the pipe's diameter as 500 mm (nominal Ду500), which under the standard Soviet-era nominal-bore-to-actual-OD convention seen throughout this roster (e.g. Ду1200->1220 mm OD, Ду700->720 mm OD, Ду1000->1020 mm OD) corresponds to an actual OD of ~529-530 mm -- i.e. the SAME number GEM stores, just mechanically converted to inches with four significant figures no source ever stated in that unit. This is not a value error, it's a unit-provenance/false-precision defect, exactly the class of issue already flagged for this row in the country note alongside P1773 and P3063. I am filling this ref (the number is corroborated) while flagging the representation issue separately for Update to fix the stored units.

fills.researcher_notes: Both sources state the combined Dashava-Kyiv-Moscow length as exactly 1301 km, matching GEM exactly. Two independent non-GEM sources.

ru.wikipedia gives the exact commissioning date '18 января 1952 года' for the Bryansk-Moscow extension. BBC corroborates the same extension/timeline (construction from 1949, gas reaching Moscow in 1951, i.e. the tail end of the same commissioning event); together they support StartYear1=1952.

Both sources state pipe diameter 500 mm nominal (=~529-530 mm actual OD under the standard Soviet Ду-to-OD convention), consistent with GEM's stored 20.87 in (=529.9 mm) -- but see the paired validity concern: no source states an inch figure, so the unit/precision is an artifact that Update should convert to metric.

Correct for the pipeline's original design purpose -- both sources describe it repeatedly as carrying Dashava-field gas ('дашавский газ'). Caveat: per the classification concern above, since the 1966 flow reversal the operative Ukrainian segment is fed via interconnection with the Shebelinka network (P1452/P2387), not directly from Dashava field gas -- flagging as historically-grounded but possibly stale for current operations, same caveat as PipelineType/EndLocation.

ru.wikipedia states the EXTENDED (post-1952) Dashava-Kyiv-Moscow pipeline's throughput capacity was 'около 2 млрд м3 в год' (~2 bcm/year), reasonably close to GEM's 1.80 bcm/y (the original pre-extension Dashava-Kyiv-only section's design capacity was much lower, 1,500,000 m3/day =~0.55 bcm/y -- do not confuse the two; that smaller figure describes only the 509.6 km first-stage section before the Moscow extension). Only one source states this precise figure so tier is medium, not high; page verification flags contains_value=false because the verifier does a literal substring match on '1.80' which the Russian-language approximate figure does not contain -- the agreement is a reasonable-rounding match, not a literal string match, and is asserted here by the researcher's own reading of the page per the confidence-tier rubric's inference guidance.
Trivially confirmed -- both sources describe this throughout as a natural gas pipeline (природный газ).

NOT filling this ref: both BBC and ru.wikipedia explicitly state that since the 1966 reconstruction the pipeline operates as a 'распределительный' (DISTRIBUTION) line for its currently-active Ukrainian segment, not a transmission trunk in the original sense. Adding a ref here would be citing sources that actually contradict the stored value's current-tense meaning. See the paired classification concern in validity[] -- routed to Update for a PipelineType/current-function review, not filled here.

StartLocation=Dashava/Lviv Oblast/Ukraine is well supported as the historical as-built origin (both sources). But EndLocation=Moscow/Russia is the part in question: since the 1966 reversal the pipeline's documented current function is a WEST-flowing Ukraine-domestic distribution line supplying Kyiv/Zhytomyr/Ternopil oblasts (BBC), not a live through-line to Moscow. Marking this UNRESOLVED rather than REFS_ADDED because the sources support the historical route but arguably contradict the CURRENT end-to-end reading of EndLocation -- see the classification concern in validity[]. Providing the refs here for Update's use regardless.

BBC (published Oct 2018) states the pipeline currently ('сейчас') supplies gas to towns/villages of Kyiv, Zhytomyr and Ternopil oblasts and speculates it will keep finding work in future -- this entails 'operating' as of 2018 by the confidence-tier rubric's status-inference guidance, even though the word 'operating' never appears. No source newer than 2018 was found confirming continued operation through 2026; no evidence of decommissioning was found either. Single source, tier low, and eight years old relative to today -- recommend a fresher confirmation in a future pass rather than treating this as settled.

summary: P1465 is a real, well-documented 1948-52 Soviet trunk (1301 km, commissioned 18 Jan 1952 -- both figures independently confirmed by BBC Ukrainian + ru.wikipedia, matching GEM exactly) but flagged CONCERN/classification: both sources state the pipeline was physically reversed and reconfigured to distribution use in 1966, so current PipelineType='transmission' and EndLocation=Moscow/Russia look stale against its documented current role as a Ukraine-domestic distribution line (Kyiv/Zhytomyr/Ternopil oblasts); also flagged CONCERN/attribution (Gazprom PJSC ownership unverified and questionable given that finding) and CONCERN/spec (Diameter=20.87in is a false-precision unit round-trip of the sourced 500/529mm figure, value not wrong but unit representation is). No duplicate found against the 39-row roster. UNRESOLVED: PipelineType ref (contradicted, not filled), EndLocation half of Location ref, Owner1/Gazprom share of the Owner ref, and Status beyond a single 2018 source.
